system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer-side review — Wattlebridge Holdings.** The recommendations below are proposed negotiating positions, not agreed terms. They rely on the supplied extracts; the underlying SPA and DD documents still need verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap, with separate protection for fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to DD and recovery security; 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; no general thresholds for separately protected categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**; the Seller’s combination could exclude meaningful cumulative losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months**; limitations potentially extend to all Claims. | **36 months** for general warranties, longer category-specific periods, and timely notified claims surviving until resolved. | **Reject the universal application and seek 36 months**, with workable notice requirements and no short proceedings deadline; latent issues may emerge after 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share general warranty caps and deadlines. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, authority, ownership, valid issue and freedom from encumbrances; **100% price cap** and longer survival. | **Seek AUD 24m cap and seven-year contractual survival**, with execution and statutory limitation mechanics checked under NSW law; ownership risk should not sit within a depleted general cap. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is identified. | An express, overriding fraud/fraudulent misrepresentation carve-out, including relevant conduct attributable to the Seller, preserving non-excludable rights. | **Insist that no cap, threshold, time bar, disclosure, knowledge or remedy restriction protects Seller fraud**; general drafting must not immunise dishonest conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope, against relevant warranties; a fixed, indexed disclosure record. | **Reject blanket and incorporation-by-reference disclosure; negotiate specific exceptions**; document availability alone does not adequately identify the risk being accepted. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including matters merely discoverable from records. | Preferably no knowledge bar; fallback limited to actual, conscious knowledge of named Buyer deal personnel, without enquiry duties or adviser imputation. | **Delete constructive/discoverable knowledge and adviser attribution**; diligence should not transfer undiscovered warranty risk to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent, although no final consent or satisfaction evidence is supplied. | A Buyer-waivable completion condition requiring effective consent and satisfaction of relevant conditions, without materially adverse changes. | **Require consent, condition-satisfaction evidence and Buyer review before Completion**, with long-stop termination rights; roughly 30% of revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; release to follow Completion. | Debt repayment through the completion waterfall and effective release of security/guarantees at Completion, supported by binding payoff and discharge arrangements. | **Reject an unsecured post-Completion promise**; deduct the debt once under the price mechanics and obtain lender-controlled discharge arrangements so the Buyer does not inherit secured debt exposure. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional bonuses omitted from funds flow and described as a Seller matter; on-costs unresolved. | Seller-funded transaction bonuses, including applicable employer on-costs, transparently reflected in completion mechanics. | **Verify entitlement and on-costs, then include a Seller-funded payment or debt-like deduction plus residual indemnity, without double counting**; omission could leave the acquired company funding the Seller’s transaction costs. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, but non-payment is not independently verified. | Verified payment status and effective vesting/assignment of all relevant SOW3 rights, plus protection against associated title, use and third-party claim losses. | **Require cleared-payment evidence and confirmatory assignment/release, backed by a broader specific indemnity**; paying an invoice alone may not resolve every IP ownership or exploitation risk. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material; access, scope and notification duties remain unknown. | Prompt investigation, preservation/containment, legal assessment of notification obligations, updates and proportionate pre-Completion risk allocation. | **Do not accept the materiality conclusion: seek a scoped specific indemnity and, if warranted, retention or completion protection**; uncertainty is not evidence of immateriality, but neither establishes a confirmed notifiable breach. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals treated as ordinary-course costs. | Review the **AUD 330,000 aggregate** commitment, timing, scope, cancellation rights and accrual status before determining treatment. | **Assess the renewals together; require Buyer approval for new/accelerated commitments and appropriate accounting treatment**; they are neither automatically ordinary-course nor automatically debt-like. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance extend across all Claims unless expressly displaced. | Express, distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, completion/price obligations and fraud. | **Insert a clear limitation matrix and overriding precedence clause**; otherwise blanket wording may silently neutralise separately negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on DD-012’s register recording Harbourglass as holder of 100%. | Independent checks of issued capital, ownership chain, encumbrances, options/convertibles and transfer restrictions, plus effective completion transfers and register updates. | **Verify title beyond the register and require supporting warranties and deliverables**; the register is evidence, not conclusive assurance of unencumbered ownership of all equity interests. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranty positions deemed settled under the general regime. | Tax covenant/indemnity for appropriate pre-Completion liabilities, statutory-period-aligned survival and claims procedures; robust IP warranties addressing ownership, licences, infringement and contractor rights. | **Expressly reserve both topics as open and negotiate separate caps, periods and exclusions where warranted**; neither the tax exposure nor the central IP risks are adequately resolved by declaring general terms settled. |

**Immediate priorities:** secure effective Bluefen consent and Riverlark discharge arrangements; resolve Ironquay title and bonus funding; investigate the incident; and prevent blanket limitations and disclosures from defeating those protections.
=== END ADVICE ===
